rationale: Both candidates converge on the same two real diff-grounded issues (the self.device_module resolved at construction rather than per-encode, and the FL2VA/Ref2VA copy-paste bug in the recipe) which only loosely overlaps the sparse ground truth (gcanlin's platform-abstraction suggestion and the request to drop an unseen UT file, neither exactly hit by either candidate). X goes further with a sophisticated, well-reasoned catch about torch.random.fork_rng's default device_type='cuda' silently mismatching non-CUDA devices — a plausible real bug beyond what either reviewer or Y surfaced, though its 'empirical test' evidence is unverifiable and slightly theatrical. Y is more conservative and uniformly evidence-quoted per finding but is phrased as hedged questions rather than directives, and misses the fork_rng issue. X's Blocking/Should-fix/Nits structure with concrete code fixes is more actionable than Y's flatter validated/sweep list.
